title: Sora 2 API Pricing Per Second and Per Plan in 2026
summary: Sora pricing works two ways: monthly plans in the app or pay-per-second via API. See which billing model fits your video generation budget.
body_markdown:
## Retries, Resolution and Limits That Inflated the Bill


By the second week the bill had grown, because every discarded take is billed at the same rate as the one you keep. **The real price is the sticker price times your attempts.**


### How discarded takes multiply Sora per-second cost


**3 attempts per usable clip** is what a shot-list project needed, where each clip stands alone, in the creator reports[Invideo](https://invideo.io/faq/what-percentage-of-ai-generated-video-clips-are-actually-2/) collected. A Sora fashion film needed 16.


> **The real price is the sticker price times your attempts.


Once scenes have to match each other, the count climbs: according to[Invideo](https://invideo.io/faq/what-percentage-of-ai-generated-video-clips-are-actually-2/) , connected scenes needed 16.67. A Kalshi ad, made for a prediction-market company, needed 26.67.


Per Invideo, a Protopica short needed 37. The more a clip has to match what came before, the more takes you throw away.


### Sora retry costs for our shot list


Because our team's shot list looked like the first case, we re-ran it at three to one.


The chart shows the cost of one usable 10-second clip at 1, 3 and 16 attempts on both tiers, which means you see immediately how much retries multiply costs.


Three attempts triples the price, and 16 attempts turns $1.00 into $16.00 on Sora 2 and $7.00 into $112.00 on Sora 2 Pro, making any trial-and-error approach prohibitively expensive.


You can't assume the cheaper tier will cost less overall: retries can outweigh the tier choice, and Pro at 3 attempts costs $21.00, more than Sora 2 at 16, which means you must calculate your specific scenario before choosing.


*(chart)*


Resolution is the other multiplier, and it stacks on the retry count.


### Sora resolution and duration cost multipliers


At $0.70 a second against $0.10, the 1080p Pro tier costs seven times the 720p Sora 2 tier for the same clip length, meaning this premium should be reserved for quality-critical work. The upgrade makes sense only for projects requiring 1080p.


Seven times the rate, times three attempts, is why the same shot list cost far more once we upgraded.


Double the length and you double the bill. Length scales it in a straight line, and a failed 20-second take wastes twice what a failed 10-second one does. Draft short and at 720p, then render the keepers at higher quality.


You will not see limits in the per-second rate, but they change what you spend. Check OpenAI's current terms for each before budgeting:


1. How many clips can render at once, since a queue slows your retries.
2. Whether a moderation refusal still consumes credit, because a refused prompt is an attempt that produced nothing.
3. Whether the watermark rules fit your use, because a clip you can't publish is a discarded take.
4. Whether prepaid credits expire, since unused balance can vanish.


Price them in before you commit, since each can add attempts or waste money.
